page.title: Fun maps
page.description: San Francisco's neighborhoods in silly-but-true maps: hometown coffee vs Starbucks, burritos vs dumplings, tennis vs pickleball, what each neighborhood calls 311 about, and where the parking tickets go.
page.lede: The same 41 neighborhoods as the map, counted in less serious ways. Each map is a head-to-head or a signature: what a neighborhood has more of than the rest of the city.
page.credits: Shops and restaurants © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). 311 requests and parking citations: DataSF (311 Cases; SFMTA Parking Citations & Fines; public domain). Rec and Park courts: San Francisco Recreation and Park Department. EV chargers: U.S. DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center. Counts are only as complete as their sources.

maps.title: What each neighborhood calls 311 about
maps.note: Each neighborhood is coloured by the kind of 311 request it makes far more often than the city as a whole, not its most common one (that's street cleaning almost everywhere). Hover or tap for the single most over-represented request. Requests about people, such as encampments, and general requests are left out.

maps.title: Parking tickets
maps.note: SFMTA's citations, placed by the neighborhood the City records for each one. A $100-odd street-cleaning ticket is San Francisco's most common by far.
